title: Like pearls strung on a single thread

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः । असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु ॥
verses.tr: The Blessed Lord says: Arjuna, fix your mind on Me, take refuge in Me, and practice yoga. Hear how you will know Me fully, without doubt.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna carries on the promise from the last verse, showing Arjuna exactly how to know him fully and without doubt.

body.text: The Blessed Lord says: Arjuna, fix your mind on Me, take refuge in Me, and practice yoga. Hear how you will know Me fully, without doubt. Krishna states three conditions for knowing him: a mind attached to me, practicing yoga, and taking refuge. The word mad-ashrayah, taking refuge in me, shows that the practice of yoga happens within the shelter of the divine. Krishna says he is the source of all knowledge and direct realization, and that knowing him leaves nothing else to be known.

verses.sa: ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः । यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते ॥
verses.tr: I will reveal to you knowledge together with direct realization in full. Knowing that, nothing more remains to be known here.
verses.angle: Jnana with vijnana ends all learning
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has asked Arjuna to fix his mind on Him. Now, He answers what that knowing actually is. Listen for the promise that ends all inquiry.

body.text: I will reveal to you knowledge together with direct realization in full. Knowing that, nothing more remains to be known here. Krishna pairs jnana with vijnana, knowledge joined to direct realization, and says he will speak it completely, so that after knowing it, nothing else remains to be known. He then says that among thousands, one may strive, and among them, one may know Him in truth.

verses.sa: मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्िचद्यतति सिद्धये । यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्िचन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ॥
verses.tr: Among thousands of people, one may strive for perfection; among those striving, one may know Me in truth.
verses.angle: Kashchit: the word of extreme rarity
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna does not promise that many will find him; he says the path is hard and the goal is rare.

body.text: Among thousands of people, one may strive for perfection; among those striving, one may know Me in truth. The word kashchit, some one, appears twice in this verse. It shows that one in thousands strives, and among those strivers, one knows Me in truth. He then moves from the rarity of knowing him to the very elements that make up his lower nature.

verses.sa: भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च । अहङ्कार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा ॥
verses.tr: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and ego: this is My eightfold lower nature.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna lists eight parts of creation. Listen for the word 'mind' and notice where it is placed in that list.

body.text: Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect, and ego: this is My eightfold lower nature. The word manas, mind, sits right between the five elements and the intellect. By placing mind among matter, Krishna shows that even our inner world belongs to the lower nature. Krishna then names the higher nature that sustains the world, beyond these eight parts.

verses.sa: अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम् । जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत् ॥
verses.tr: Know My higher nature, which is different from this lower nature, O mighty-armed one. By that living nature, this world is sustained.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just listed the material world. Now he points past it. Listen for the living force that keeps everything together.

body.text: Know My higher nature, which is different from this lower nature, O mighty-armed one. By that living nature, this world is sustained. Krishna asks Arjuna to know his higher nature, jivabhutam, become living. The lower nature is matter and mind, but the higher nature is a living power that sustains the world. Krishna now declares that all beings spring from these two natures, and he is their source and end.

verses.sa: एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय । अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा ॥
verses.tr: Know that all beings are born from these two natures. I am the source and the dissolution of the entire universe.
verses.angle: Prabhavah and pralayastatha: origin and end
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues by explaining how every living thing is born, and then states his own position in all of it.

body.text: Know that all beings are born from these two natures. I am the source and the dissolution of the entire universe. Krishna uses the word prabhavah, source, and pralayastatha, dissolution also. In one breath, he holds the beginning and the end of the universe as his own. Krishna now makes his claim absolute, saying nothing is higher than him in all the world.

verses.sa: मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय । मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ॥
verses.tr: O Dhananjaya, nothing exists higher than Me. All this world is strung on Me like pearls on a thread.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: After explaining the two natures, Krishna now asks Arjuna to see the whole world in one image. Listen for the single word that holds the universe together.

body.text: O Dhananjaya, nothing exists higher than Me. All this world is strung on Me like pearls on a thread. Notice the word protam, meaning strung. The entire world is not just near him, it is woven through him like beads on a thread, held in place only by that single line. Krishna then lists his form in the elements, the syllables, and the qualities of human beings.

verses.sa: रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभास्मि शशिसूर्ययोः । प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु ॥
verses.tr: O son of Kunti, I am the taste in water, the light in the moon and sun, the syllable Om in all the Vedas, the sound in space, and the valor in human beings.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna now speaks to Arjuna, showing how he is the very life in ordinary things. Listen for the first thing he names.

body.text: O son of Kunti, I am the taste in water, the light in the moon and sun, the syllable Om in all the Vedas, the sound in space, and the valor in human beings. The first word, rasah, means taste in water, and Krishna claims it as his own. He is the flavor that makes water life-giving, right there in the water Arjuna drinks. Krishna then names the light in the moon and sun, the sound in space, and the strength in human beings.

verses.sa: पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ । जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु ॥
verses.tr: I am the pure fragrance in the earth, the radiance in fire, the life in all beings, and the austerity in ascetics.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Listen for one word that names a quality found in people who deny themselves. Notice how Krishna claims it as his own.

body.text: I am the pure fragrance in the earth, the radiance in fire, the life in all beings, and the austerity in ascetics. Listen for tapah, austerity. It means the heat of discipline, the burning energy of those who fast, meditate, and restrain the body. Krishna says he is this heat in the very people who practice it. He then tells Arjuna to know him as the eternal seed of all beings.

verses.sa: बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम् । बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् ॥
verses.tr: Know Me, O Partha, as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the intelligence of the intelligent and the brilliance of the brilliant.
verses.angle: Sanatana, the eternal seed of all beings
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just shown that he is the fragrance in the earth and the radiance in fire. Now he names his own origin. Listen for the source he names for all beings and for the qualities he holds in people.

body.text: Know Me, O Partha, as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the intelligence of the intelligent and the brilliance of the brilliant. He calls himself the seed, sanatana, eternal, of all beings, and then says he is the intelligence in the intelligent and the brilliance in the brilliant, so every clear mind and bright strength comes from him. He now moves from the source of life to the source of strength, naming what he is in those who are strong.

verses.sa: बलं बलवतामस्मि कामरागविवर्जितम् । धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ ॥
verses.tr: Among the strong, I am strength free from desire and attachment. In beings, I am desire that does not oppose dharma, O best of the Bharatas.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna continues describing his nature, and this time he takes two opposites and makes them his own. Listen for how he redefines them.

body.text: Among the strong, I am strength free from desire and attachment. In beings, I am desire that does not oppose dharma, O best of the Bharatas. Krishna says he is strength, balam, but not ordinary strength, balavatam, of the strong; he is that strength free from craving. He also says he is desire, kamah, but only desire that does not oppose dharma. Sattva, rajas, and tamas are not outside him, but live inside him.

verses.sa: ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये । मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि नत्वहं तेषु ते मयि ॥
verses.tr: Know that all states of being, sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic, arise from Me. I am not in them; they are in Me.
verses.angle: sattva, rajas, tamas all come from Krishna but he stays beyond them
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna asks what state of mind or nature any person truly comes from. Listen for his answer about where all qualities begin.

body.text: Know that all states of being, sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic, arise from Me. I am not in them; they are in Me. Krishna says that sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic states all arise from him. Yet he is not contained within them, because they rest in him and he remains beyond them. Krishna then explains that the whole world is deluded by those same qualities and does not know him as the imperishable one beyond them.

verses.sa: त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत् । मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम् ॥
verses.tr: Deluded by these three qualities, the whole world does not know me, who am beyond them and imperishable.
verses.angle: Mohitam: the world is deluded by the gunas
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna says the world is caught in nature's qualities and cannot recognize who is beyond them. Listen for the word that names this trap.

body.text: Deluded by these three qualities, the whole world does not know me, who am beyond them and imperishable. Listen for the word mohitam, deluded. It names the state of being trapped by the three qualities so tightly that the world cannot recognize Krishna as the imperishable reality outside them. Krishna then says this divine illusion is hard to cross, and only those who take refuge in Him go beyond it.
